data.short_meaning: God of Wealth, Lord of Fortune
data.long_meaning: Banshidhar is a combination of two Sanskrit words - Ban, meaning lord or god, and Shidhar, meaning wealth. It is a name that signifies the god of wealth and the lord of fortune. This name is believed to bring prosperity, wealth, and good fortune to the one who bears it. The name Banshidhar carries the meaning “God of Wealth, Lord of Fortune” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Banshidhar usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wealth, lord of fortune and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Banshidhar is a name that is deeply rooted in Hindu spirituality. It is a name that signifies the presence of the god of wealth and prosperity in one's life. It is believed that this name brings blessings of abundance, wealth, and good fortune.
data.etymology: Banshidhar belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Wealth, Lord of Fortune.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Banshidhar total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Banshidhar is commonly found in Hindu communities, especially in India. It is a name that reflects the Hindu faith's emphasis on the importance of wealth and prosperity in life. In Hindu culture, gods and goddesses are believed to bestow wealth and blessings upon their devotees. Banshidhar is a name that embodies this belief and highlights the connection between the divine and material aspects of life.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Banshidhar lies in its meaning— lord of wealth or god of prosperity. It is a name that invokes the blessings of deities associated with wealth and prosperity, such as Laxmi, Ganesha, and Vishnu. Christianity has its saint for prosperity, and Hinduism has its deities. In Hindu philosophy, spiritual growth and material wealth are not mutually exclusive. Instead, they are interconnected, and one leads to the other. Thus, the name Banshidhar signifies not only the material aspect of wealth but also the spiritual aspect of seeking blessings from the divine to fulfill one's material and spiritual needs. It is a reminder that wealth is not just an end goal but a means to lead a contented and fulfilling life.

historical_references.reference: Banshidhar Tewari (1879-1955) was a prominent Indian scholar and writer who contributed significantly to the study of Indian philosophy and culture. He authored numerous books on various aspects of Indian thought and was a leading figure in the revival of interest in Indian philosophy in the 20th century.

Banshidhar Choudhury (1883-1951) was a renowned freedom fighter, politician and journalist in British India. He was a close associate of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and played a key role in the Indian National Army (INA) during World War II. He was imprisoned by the British for his political activities and later became the Chief Minister of Tripura State in Independent India.
